Cache Eviction (Final Interview Version)
✅ What is Cache Eviction?
Cache eviction is the process of removing data from the cache when it becomes full or when data is no longer valid, so that new data can be stored.
👉 Think of cache like a small bookshelf — when it’s full, you must decide which book to remove.

✅ 🔷 Types of Cache Eviction

✅ 1. LRU (Least Recently Used) ⭐ Most Important
👉 Removes the item that has not been used for the longest time
✅ Example
Cache Size = 3

Access: A, B, C
Cache: [A, B, C]

Access A again
Cache: [B, C, A]

Add D → remove B
Cache: [C, A, D]

✅ Used in: Redis, OS, Java caches
✅ Key idea: Old unused data is removed

✅ 2. LFU (Least Frequently Used)
👉 Removes the item with the lowest access frequency
✅ Example
A → used 10 times
B → used 2 times
C → used 1 time

Add D → remove C

✅ Use case: Hot/frequently accessed data

✅ 3. FIFO (First In First Out)
👉 Removes the oldest inserted item
✅ Example
Insert: A, B, C
Cache: [A, B, C]

Add D → remove A
Cache: [B, C, D]

✅ Simple but not smart

✅ 4. Random Eviction
👉 Removes a random item
✅ Advantage: Fast
❌ Disadvantage: May remove useful data

✅ 5. TTL (Time-To-Live / Expiry)**
👉 Each entry has a time limit
✅ Example
User Data TTL = 10 minutes

After 10 mins → removed automatically

✅ Used for: sessions, API responses

✅ 6. MRU (Most Recently Used)
👉 Removes the most recently accessed item
✅ Example
Access: A, B, C
Access C (most recent)

Add D → remove C

✅ Rare use case

✅ 🔷 Easy Memory Trick 🧠
FIFO → First in, first out
LRU → Least recently used leaves
LFU → Least frequently used leaves
MRU → Most recently used leaves
TTL → Leaves after time expires
Random → Anyone can leave


✅ 🔷 What Interviewers Expect
You must know:
✅ LRU (MOST IMPORTANT)
✅ LFU
✅ TTL
✅ When to use each

✅ 🔷 Java / Real Systems Context
In real systems (Redis, Caffeine, etc.), we configure:
- Max cache size
- Expire after write (TTL)
- Expire after access
- Eviction policy (LRU / LFU)


✅ 🔷 Perfect Interview Answer

“Cache eviction is the process of removing entries from cache when it becomes full or data expires.
 Common strategies include LRU, which removes least recently used items; LFU, which removes
  least frequently used items;
  FIFO, which removes oldest entries; and TTL-based eviction, 
  where data is automatically removed 
after a fixed duration.”



Imagine a library with only 3 seats:

FIFO → "First person who came leaves first."
LRU → "Person who hasn't read for the longest time leaves."
LFU → "Person who reads the least leaves."
MRU → "Person who just sat down leaves."
TTL → "Everyone has a timer; when it ends, they must leave."
Random → "The librarian picks someone randomly."
